Issue #1
60+ unique digital product ideas for every niche
Digital Products Commerce Monetize Your List
Dana Nicole
13 min read
Unique digital product ideas for your niche
Watch on

What digital product will you sell?
Picture this: you wake up in the morning and have a million items to check off your to-do list. Client work, content creation, product development, accounting, inbox management…you get the idea.
If you’re like most creators, the above situation isn’t difficult to imagine; you live it every day.
Wouldn’t it be nice (read: amazing) if you worked less and earned more money?
Enter digital products.
Digital products offer creators the ability to earn scalable passive income. But the hardest part of getting a passive income strategy in place? Coming up with profitable digital product ideas to take your passive income to new heights.
Which is why today, I'm sharing 60+ digital products to sell, regardless of your niche, so you can create a unique digital product your audience loves.
Digital product ideas to sell online
If you aren’t sure what you’d like to create, you can go through this list in its entirety. Otherwise, feel free to use the navigation below to skip straight to the different types of digital products:
Photography and videography
Educational resources
Templates
Design
Recordings
Tech
Start selling within minutes
As a creator, you deserve to get paid for your work. ConvertKit Commerce is ready-made to help you sell digital products.
Get paid with ConvertKit Commerce
Photography and videography
If you’re a shutterbug, there are many types of digital products you can put together for your audience.
Stock photos
We’re all tired of seeing the same old cheesy stock photos. Turn your lens toward shooting stock images that stand out. You can charge a monthly fee (like ConvertKit creator Alicia does with Pixistock ), or you can do a pay-per-download model.
Alicia charges a membership fee to access her library of stock photos and graphics. Image via Pixistock
You can shoot a wide range of stock photography images or choose a niche, like animals, holidays, or sports.
Stock videos
85% of businesses use video as a marketing tool (up from 61% in 2016), but not all small businesses can afford custom videography.
And as more businesses turn to video, so will the demand for affordable solutions.
ConvertKit creator, Chic Voyage Productions, offers unique travel stock videos of different cities around the world. I love how niche his content is; it shows how you don’t need to cast a wide net to catch big fish!
Chic Voyage Productions offers travel stock videos. Image via Chic Voyage Productions
Other digital product ideas if you are interested in photography/videography:
Lightroom mobile presets
After Effects templates
Video LUTs
Mockup images
Mockup videos
Scene creator
Calendar with your photography
Educational resources
Some people learn best by reading. Others prefer video courses or podcasts.
My point? There are a variety of different ways you can teach your audience something. And as a bonus, you’d don’t need to be physically present to teach your audience.
Let’s talk about different digital products to sell if you want to teach.
eBooks
eBooks are fantastic digital products to sell. You can sell them on your website or upload them to Amazon for a wider reach.
I decided to take a few modules from my eCourse and turn it into an affordable eBook. This way, I can reach my audience members who aren’t ready – or didn’t want to – commit to a course.
An eBook I sell. Image via Dana Nicole Designs
Tutorials
Putting an entire course together is time-consuming. If you want to teach but aren’t ready to put a full course together, consider selling tutorials. Tutorials are a great way to teach a portion of what you know to your followers.
ConvertKit creator Roots & Wings Furniture offers a video tutorial. Image via Roots & Wings Furniture
A tutorial can be a standalone product or part of a bigger online course if you want to up-sell at the end of the tutorial.
Courses
If you’re teaching a complex subject, a simple tutorial might not be enough to dig in.
You can offer video courses to dive into complicated subject matters through:
Powerpoint slides
Audio recordings
Video recordings
By offering video courses, you’re giving that feeling of what it would be like to be there live with you without the cost of hosting a live class.
Courses offered by Meera Kothand. Image via Meera Kothand
ConvertKit member, Meera Kothand, sells a variety of digital products, including video courses. Since she has pre-recorded her lessons, she can offer several courses simultaneously without needing to go live for any of them.
Email courses
If recording your voice or being on camera doesn’t float your boat, you’ll love this digital product idea: email courses.
Email courses give you direct access to your reader in their inbox where you can deliver:
Text-based content
Links (to external resources or videos)
Attachments
This email course from one of our ConvertKit members helps web designers streamline their process. Image via pinkpot studio
Email courses are ideal if you don’t want to set up a course portal for your students to access the material.
Membership site
You might have years of experience and backlogs of videos, audios, or written lessons. Or maybe you have content you want to produce over time, but you don’t want to wait to get students in the door.
Membership sites are the ideal way to drip large amounts of content over time to an invested audience who comes back month over month.
Charge a monthly or yearly fee for students to access your membership site. Image via Practically Enlightened You
ConvertKit member Sharon, with Practically Enlightened You, sells a yoga membership to her audience where they receive livestream and recorded classes.
Meal plans
If you're one of those savvy cooks who have your meal plans written up and recipes all ready to go each week, consider packaging custom meal plans for your readers. Meal plan and recipe packages range from monthly subscription models to one-time downloads.
You can charge a one-time or monthly subscription fee to create meal plans based on budget, diet, seasonality, and more. Image via Ultimate Meal Plans.
Other digital product ideas if you are interested in creating a resource:
Online workshops/webinars
Workout plans/videos
Digital cookbooks
Templates
On days when my to-do list feels never-ending, templates save my sanity. Templates are one of the most popular digital products. On Etsy alone, there are over half a million monthly searches for the term “templates”.
Let’s look at some of the different templates you can offer.
Legal templates
Put that law school degree to use and help your audience protect themselves with legal disclaimers. Templates can range from copyright infringement text for the bottom of a website to fully-blown customizable contracts.
Legal templates from Sam Vander Wielen. Image via Sam Vander Wielen
Sam Vander Wielen is a former lawyer turned digital entrepreneur (and ConvertKit creator!) who shares her legal knowledge through templates and trainings.
Instagram templates
On-brand Instagram Stories are challenging to create with Instagram’s native story editor. Not only are your font choices limited, but without hexadecimal color codes, it’s difficult to select branded colors.
Instagram Story templates solve the above challenges by giving users the ability to create stunning stories without knowing design. Using Instagram Story Templates, the end-user adds their own text, color, and imagery to the template and uploads it straight to their Stories.
Instagram templates are a popular digital product. Image via Allie Bjerk
